fields.h1: Build a Harassment Complaint Form That Reaches the Right Person
fields.hero_description: Build a harassment complaint form that records each incident, routes it around the person named, and tracks the case to close.
fields.features_heading: What HR Needs From the First Report
fields.features_subheading: These six parts turn a harassment complaint form into a case that has an owner and ends in a decision.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow who is involved

Pick a manager or someone outside the company, and the form asks what matters next: the reporting line for a manager, or the client and the place of contact for an outsider.
fields.feature_2:
Routing around the person named

Each report goes to the person who should open it. A report that names a manager reaches the HR director by email instead of moving up that manager's own reporting line.
fields.feature_3:
One entry per incident, as many as it takes

The reporter adds each incident on its own, with the date, the place, what was said or done, and who saw it. A pattern of remarks reads as a dated list, not one long paragraph.
fields.feature_4:
Screenshots kept with the account

The reporter can attach screenshots of text messages and emails. Each file stays on the report it belongs to, so nobody is digging through an inbox for it weeks later.
fields.feature_5:
A case record from the first submit

Every report becomes a row in a database you own, with an owner and a status. HR can see at a glance which cases are open and which have gone quiet since their last update.
fields.feature_6:
Code export when HR has its own systems

On paid plans, export the whole codebase to your GitHub repository and host it next to the systems your HR records already live in. Keep building on that code from there.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Complaint Starts, and Who Opens It
fields.tab_content_1:
When the report names her lead, Benedetta reads it first

Three months of remarks about her clothes came before a Vantor Labs analyst filed. She picks her team lead from the list of people involved and adds 4 dated incidents. Any report that names a manager skips that manager's reporting line and goes to Benedetta, the HR director, by email. She opens it that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_2:
From her phone, the table 14 report reaches Yusuf by close

Saturday dinner at Marigold Bistro ran late, and a customer at table 14 grabbed a server's arm twice. She files from her phone after the shift and picks a customer as the person involved. Reports about customers go straight to Yusuf, the general manager, by email. He has this one before the dining room closes.
fields.tab_content_3:
Complaints from Reno reach Seraphine in the West region

Six warehouses, one form: every Wren Logistics report carries the site it came from. A picker at the Reno warehouse reports a coworker's comments over the floor radio. Reno is in the West region, so the report goes to Seraphine, the HR partner for that region. Reports from the other sites go to their own partners.
fields.tab_content_4:
Fourteen quiet days return a case to Thaddeus

Dovecote Credit Union gives every complaint a case owner and tracks when it last moved. A case from the Main Street branch has gone 17 days without an update. Any case with no update in 14 days goes back on the list of Thaddeus, the HR director, and this one is 3 days past it. He asks its owner what comes next.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Harassment Complaint Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a harassment complaint form that gets each report to someone who can act on it, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for one incident at a time
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the people a report might name, from coworkers and managers to customers and vendors. Each choice opens its own follow-up questions. A report about a customer needs the table or account, while one about a manager needs the reporting line.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give every incident its own entry: when and where it happened, the words or actions involved, and any witnesses. Let the reporter add as many as they need. A dated list is far easier to look into than one long account written from memory.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide who receives each kind of report and how. Send anything naming a manager to the HR director rather than up that manager's line. Name a backup for when the first person is away, or is the person the report names.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the message the reporter sees after submitting. Say who will read the report and when to expect contact. Promise only what your process can keep: if HR may need to share details to look into a complaint, the message should not say otherwise.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the incident fields and the routing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form and the case view HR works from, with the database behind both. When a question needs to change later, ask for the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give every report a case record
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each case an owner and the date of its last update. A case list sorted by days since update shows which complaints have gone quiet. A reminder can go to the HR director once a case passes a limit you set.
fields.howto_step_7_des: File a made-up complaint that names a manager. Check that the email reaches the HR director and not the manager, and that the case shows up in the list with the right owner and status. Delete the test case when you are done.

faq_plan.q: What is a harassment complaint form?
faq_plan.a: A harassment complaint form is the written record a worker uses to report harassment to the employer. It names who was involved and their role, describes each incident with its date and place, and lists anyone who saw it. HR uses it to open a case and decide what to do next.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a harassment complaint form?
faq_plan.a: Decide who a report might name, what each incident entry asks, and who should read each kind of report. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. The result is a form employees file online, with every report saved as a case HR can assign and track.

faq_plan.q: What should a harassment complaint form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the reporter's contact details and preferred way to be reached. Add the person involved and their role, then one section per incident with the date, place, and what happened. Finish with witnesses and attachments. End with a line on what happens after the form is submitted.

faq_plan.q: Should a sexual harassment complaint form be separate from other complaints?
faq_plan.hint: Should you use a sexual harassment complaint form?
faq_plan.a: It can be either. A separate form lets you ask questions specific to sexual harassment and send those reports to a reviewer trained for them. Folding it into a general complaint form keeps one place to report, with the harassment questions appearing only when someone picks that category. On a printed harassment complaint form pdf, every reporter sees every section instead.

faq_plan.q: Where should a harassment complaint form send reports that name a manager?
faq_plan.hint: What is the required sexual harassment complaint form?
faq_plan.a: To someone outside that manager's reporting line, such as the HR director or a second named contact. Make the role of the person involved a pick list, not free text, because a routing rule can match a fixed choice more cleanly than a typed title. Then add a backup contact for when the first one is the person named.

faq_plan.q: Can employees attach evidence to a harassment complaint form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an upload field for screenshots of texts and emails, plus a text box for anything that cannot be attached, such as where a voicemail is saved. Emergent builds the upload step from the same prompt as the form, and every file stays attached to its case.

faq_plan.q: How do you check the dates on a harassment complaint form?
faq_plan.a: Compare each incident date with the schedule for that week. If shifts are logged through a time sheet form, those records show who worked alongside the reporter that day, which tells HR whom to talk to first. Treat a mismatch as a question to ask the reporter, not as proof either way.

faq_plan.q: Should a harassment complaint form ask what outcome the reporter wants?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as an optional question. Knowing what the reporter hopes for, such as a schedule change or a meeting with HR, helps the reviewer plan the next step. Say plainly on the form that HR decides the outcome after it looks into the report.

faq_plan.q: How do you keep cases from a harassment complaint form from stalling?
faq_plan.a: Give each complaint an owner and a last-update date, then set a limit in days. A case that passes the limit goes back to the HR director with an email reminder. Emergent builds the case list and that reminder from the same prompt that describes the form.

faq_plan.q: How is a harassment complaint form different from a grievance?
faq_plan.a: A harassment complaint form records conduct by one specific person, such as remarks or unwanted contact. A grievance form covers wider workplace disputes, such as pay or scheduling. One intake can serve both, with a category question that opens the harassment fields only when someone picks them.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank sheets: a presbytery PDF, a school district Word file, a Title IX PDF, a California form on SHRM, an Australian legal template, and two template sites. Every one stops at the filled-in page. None says who opens the report, what happens when the person named is the reporter's own manager, or how HR keeps a case moving. This page is for the HR team building the intake: questions that change with who is involved, routing that goes around the person named, every incident date and witness on one record, and a case list that flags a complaint left without an update.
